subject: Demo recap & proposed 4-week POC — Pinecrest Analytics evaluation checklist and owners
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Novak <sara@pinecrest.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap & proposed 4-week POC — Pinecrest Analytics evaluation checklist and owners

Hi Sara — thanks again for carving out time yesterday. Quick recap + a concrete POC proposal so the team has something to react to.

Recap from the demo (high-level)
- Ingest: Pinecrest will point Redwood at a subset (100k) of anonymized clinical notes via S3.
- Use case: extract structured problem/medication entities + question-answering for triage teams.
- Success focus: precision on entity extraction and latency to support real-time triage flows.

Proposed 4-week POC (outline)
Week 0 (prep): sign SOW, exchange test credentials, finalize sample dataset and access.
Week 1: onboarding + ingest + baseline runs (Redwood default configs).
Week 2: tuning (batching, KV caching, quantization profile) + run evals on our shared prompt suite.
Week 3: integration tests with your triage staging app (simulated traffic).
Week 4: acceptance, handoff + playbook for production rollout.

Proposed success criteria (starter) — we’ll validate these together:
- Entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 on the annotated subset.
- Average inference latency (tailored test) < 200ms (95th perc < 300ms) for 512-token seqs.
- Throughput: sustain 15 qps with auto-batching while staying under the latency targets.
- No PII leakage in logs; all customer data stays in your S3 and Redwood’s ephemeral compute (we’ll include the private deployment option in SOW).

Owners (suggested)
- Redwood PM: Ben Carter — overall engagement and schedule.
- Redwood Ops/Eng lead: Jordan Blake — technical onboarding, performance tuning.
- Pinecrest PM: Sara Novak — dataset approvals, acceptance sign-off.
- Pinecrest Procurement: procurement@pinecrest.ai — contracting.

Attachments: I’ve attached a compact success criteria workbook, a draft SOW, and a technical intake template to speed intake.

Next steps — please:
1) Confirm owners and a preferred POC kickoff week (our recommendation: week of Jul 2).
2) Procurement contact to confirm SOW timing or redlines.
3) If the technical team wants a pre-kickoff sync, Jordan is available next Tue/Wed.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to walk through the checklist.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful and concrete. Appreciate the checklist. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Owners: confirmed — I’ll be the PM and procurement@pinecrest.ai will own contracting. I’ve looped Tom (external advisor) because he’ll help validate the evaluation metrics on the triage integration.
2) Timeline: Jul 2 start works for the product team; procurement asked if we can target an executed SOW by Jun 30. Is that feasible on your side?
3) Data: we’ll prepare an anonymized 100k object S3 bucket and share a short manifest next week.

We’d like to add one metric to the acceptance criteria: average token cost per inference should be under $0.003 for the evaluated prompt set — can Redwood provide an estimate based on the initial baseline runs?

I’m available for a quick alignment call Mon (Jun 25) afternoon PT if you want to walk through the SOW and checklist before procurement reviews.

Adding a couple of technical clarifications from Redwood ops so expectations are clear before kickoff: 

Technical intake and test harness
- Jordan will send the technical intake template filled with our baseline compute profile and a sample ingest manifest.
- For the triage integration, please confirm the staging app endpoint and expected payload shape; we prefer to run synthetic traffic to match 80th / 95th perc loads.

Performance targets (concrete test definitions)
- Latency test: 10k single-request runs with realistic prompt distribution, measure p50/p95/p99. Acceptance uses p95 < 300ms for the triage test; target p50 < 120ms.
- Throughput test: ramp from 1 qps to 20 qps across 15m window — POC passes if average latency remains within acceptance band and error rate < 1%.
- Quality test: use your annotated subset (n=2,500) for entity F1 and the prompt suite (n=500) for QA accuracy.

Cost telemetry and billing
- We will enable token-level telemetry during the POC for visibility; that will provide the cost estimate Sara requested. We’ll include a sample cost report after Week 1 baseline runs.

Jordan will take the lead for technical onboarding: jordan.blake@redwood.ai — he’ll propose a pre-kickoff slot Tue/Wed next week.

Marissa Cole
